name: OPERA
notes: Detector, site, result and document links are derived from the records that reference this experiment and are not stored here.
The detector is hosted at site:lngs-hall-c (LNGS Hall C); the placement is recorded on detector:opera and the beam on beamline:cngs.
The INSPIRE experiment-registry identifier is not recorded for OPERA; none has been looked up.

The original OPERA website (operaweb.lngs.infn.it) did not resolve when checked on 2026-09-17 and lngs.infn.it/en/opera returned HTTP 500, so no website link is recorded; the experiment's own news page is cited from an Internet Archive capture of 2021-01-25.
The atlas holds one result record for OPERA, the 2015 discovery paper; no technical-design or other document record has been written for it.

physics_goals.quote: The OPERA experiment was designed to search for νµ → ντ oscillations in appearance mode, i.e. by detecting the τ leptons produced in charged current ντ interactions.
physics_goals.value: Directly observe muon-neutrino to tau-neutrino oscillation in appearance mode over a long baseline

summary.plain: An experiment in a mountain tunnel in Italy that caught neutrinos fired 732 kilometres through the Earth from CERN in Switzerland. Its photographic-film-and-lead detector directly caught tau neutrinos appearing from a beam that started as muon neutrinos, proving they change type over the trip.
summary.technical: Emulsion-cloud-chamber (lead/nuclear-emulsion 'brick') experiment in LNGS Hall C, receiving the CNGS muon-neutrino beam from the CERN SPS over a 732 km baseline. Took data 2008-2012 and reported discovery of νμ → ντ appearance at 5.1σ significance (the paper's abstract says larger than 5σ) from five candidate tau-neutrino interactions, confirming long-baseline neutrino oscillation in appearance mode.
